records.title: Concern over absence of tigers in Kawal Tiger Reserve of Adilabad district of Telangana.
details:
Shri S Niranjan Reddy: According
to the All India Tiger Estimation of India (AITE) conducted in 2018 and 2022,
there are no resident tiger populations in the Kawal Tiger Reserve, Telangana.
While India?s overall tiger population has reached 3682 as of 2023, Telangana
lags behind with an alarmingly low population of only 21 tigers. The Kawal
Tiger Reserve, having a large reserve area of 2000 km2, is reduced as a
dispersal corridor rather than a breeding habitat. In Kawal Tiger Reserve, the
tigers frequently enter from TadobaAndhari Tiger Reserve and Tipeshwar Wildlife
Sanctuary by crossing the Pranahitha River.However, due to loss of habitat,
prey and poaching, tiger dispersal often results in conflict-related deaths.
Such deaths are exacerbated by severe corridor fragmentation from
encroachments, agriculture and infrastructure. Moreover, National Green
Tribunal (NGT) in a 2024 suo moto case, observed that extensive tribal
encroachments for podu cultivation has reduced forest and corridor space in
Kawal Tiger Reserve. According to National Tiger Conservation Authority
(NTCA)?s 2024 Report, there are chronic staff shortages, weak protection
infrastructure and lack of wildlife health systems, alongside delays in village
relocation and corridor protection. Inadequate community engagement and slow
adoption of technology continue to undermine effective patrolling and tiger
conservation. Building on the proven success of Project Tiger, I urge the
Central Government to strengthen conservation at Kawal Tiger Reserve by issuing
advisories to the State forest department. The government should further
undertake a science-based reintroduction and monitoring framework, supported by
clear accountability and annual performance audits.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand to improve Nagpur-Adilabad-Nirmal-Hyderabad Railway Connectivity.
details:
Shri S Niranjan Reddy: I bring
to attention of the Government a matter of great importance to the people of
Nirmal and surrounding regions. There is a long-standing demand for improved
rail connectivity between Nagpur and Hyderabad, particularly through the
proposed Adilabad-Nirmal-Armoor railway line. This vital line would directly connect
Nirmal to major cities like Nagpur, Adilabad and Hyderabad. In 2023, the
Railway Board instructed a survey for a railway line from Patancheruvu to
Adilabad, passing through towns like Nizamabad, Armoor and Nirmal. Furthermore,
the survey for the Armoor-Adilabad line via Nirmal was already completed in
2010-11. The implementation of the railway line is yet to materialize despite
two surveys ordered by the Government. A new 136 km rail line between Adilabad
and Armoor via Nirmal will directly connect major cities like Nagpur and
Hyderabad. Presently, there is only one train linking Adilabad and Hyderabad.
However, this train passes through Maharashtra. Passengers have to travel 435 km
through Maharashtra to reach Hyderabad due to the lack of a direct railway
line. The road distance between Adilabad and Hyderabad is only 300 km. The new
rail line will provide a direct connection between Adilabad and Hyderabad. It
will greatly reduce travel time and benefit both passenger and freight
transportation. The demand for the Adilabad-Nirmal-Armoor railway line has been
pending for the last 50 years. With a population of 7 lakh, Nirmal district
faces significant challenges due to the absence of railway connectivity. I urge
the government to expedite the sanction and funding of this crucial project.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over decline of Single-Screen theatres in India.
details:
Shri S Niranjan Reddy:India?s cinema culture is facing an unprecedented crisis. One
research shows that India now has fewer than 6,000 single-screen theatres, as
compared to 25,000 theatres in the 1990s. In May 2024, this
crisis worsened as 450 single screens in Telangana were shut down temporarily
due to extremely low footfalls. There are several reasons for this collapse.
Multiplex expansion, high production and distribution costs, rising ticket
prices, and the pandemic-driven shift to OTT (Over The Top) platforms have
steadily eroded theatre audiences. For single screens in smaller towns, high
operational expenses and limited access to credit have pushed many to permanent
closure. An affordability crisis is also looming around single-screen theatres.
This is driven by surge-priced tickets, 18% GST, platform fees, and exorbitant
F&B rates. While the industry cites a national average ticket price of
₹130, the urban reality is starkly different: PVR INOX?s average ticket
price reached ₹254 in Q1 FY26, alongside record food spending. Yet even
multiplexes are struggling, posting a ₹114.3 crore loss in FY24,
revealing a model that neither sustains audiences nor businesses. This moment
calls for urgent policy action: GST relief for single screens, concessional
loans-renovation support, rational regulation of concession pricing, and swift
single-window theatre clearances. Without timely intervention, India risks
losing a cultural institution that has shaped generations. I urge the
Government to look into it.
(ENDS)

records.title: Increase in Anti-microbial Resistance in India
details:
Shri
S Niranjan Reddy: Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) is a growing problem in India
with an increase of 5 to 10 percent in resistance levels for broad-spectrum
antibiotics. Factors such as the indiscriminate use of antibiotics, easy
over-the-counter availability and the misuse of strong antibiotic-based
treatment for common infections are exacerbating the AMR crisis. Treatment of
infectious diseases like E.Coli and K. pneumonia has become exceptionally
challenging due to the resistance to antibiotics like Imipenem. According to a
WHO report, India ranks high in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and
drug-resistant typhoid cases, posing immense difficulties in effective
treatment due to the emergence of AMR. ICMR Report also flags this as a major
concern. The new National Action Plan 2.0 for AMR is pending finalisation and
may have to be unveiled expeditiously to tackle this problem. Prominent medical
professionals have warned that AMR in India has the potential to trigger the
next epidemic. Failure to address this issue urgently will result in severe
consequences, including prolonged hospital stays, escalated treatment expenses,
heightened post-treatment healthcare costs, and, most importantly, a grave
threat to human life. Thus, I request the Central Government to swiftly
prioritize and implement decisive measures to combat AMR with utmost urgency.
(Ends)

records.title: The Need to Bridge the AI and Data Science Skill Gap in India
details:
Shri S Niranjan Reddy: Data
science skills are crucial for AI development and deployment. However,
presently India has an acute shortage of trained AI and data science
professionals. As per a NASSCOM report from 2023, there is a significant supply
gap of 60% - 73% for specialised roles like machine learning engineers, data
scientists, AI researchers and data engineers. As of 2022, India had a
shortfall of 213,000 general AI and data science professionals, indicating a
51% supply gap.Notably, 70% of Indias AI talent is concentrated in Tier 1
cities, highlighting the need to promote Tier 2 and 3 cities as new hubs for AI
development.To address this, the government should update and integrate AI and
data science into educational curricula at all levels. Industry-academia
collaborations should be fostered to promote joint research projects and
innovation hubs aligned with industry needs. The Future Skills Prime program
could expand ties with AI-powered learning platforms to offer free personalized
training and real-time feedback.Government initiatives like the India AI
Mission should emphasize continuous learning and professional development. This
can be achieved through fellowships, investing in higher education and
research, incubating startups, providing mentorship and engaging in international
collaborations.AI adoption could add up to $500 billion to Indias GDP by 2025,
accounting for 10% of the countrys $5 trillion economy goal. Therefore, it is
crucial for the government to take necessary steps to ensure a skilled
workforce is available for AI development in India.
(Ends)

records.title: Harnessing AI in primary education focusing on government school readiness for integrating new technology effectively.
details:
Shri
S Niranjan Reddy:
The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in primary education holds
immense potential to revolutionize learning by offering personalized and
adaptive experiences. AI promises to transform education by improving
engagement, accessibility, and administrative efficiency. It ensures equitable
access to quality education, especially for students with disabilities and
learning challenges, preparing them for a technology-driven future. A
comprehensive National Framework for AI in Education should be developed along
with partnerships from the private sector to fund for effective implementation.
The National Education Technology Forum (NETF) must accelerate its efforts by
organizing regional and national conferences, sharing best practices and
creating guidelines for AI tools in education. Platforms like DIKSHA and SWAYAM
portal should incorporate AI to provide personalized learning, enhance teacher
training and reduce administrative burdens. Additionally, tools like Anuvadini,
developed by AICTE, can be integrated into these educational portals to provide
multilingual content. Enhancing digital literacy and AI training programs for
teachers will significantly improve their ability to integrate AI into their
teaching practices. As per Government data in 2023, only 24% of government
schools have internet access, and just 37% have functional computers. Reliable
electricity remains a major issue, particularly in rural areas. By investing in
robust internet connectivity and digital infrastructure, creating smart classes,
upgrading existing computer labs in schools, particularly in underserved areas,
India can ensure that all students benefit from AI-driven educational
innovations. I urge Government to look into it.
(Ends)
